reason: The text contains several regular human characters with spoken dialogue and clear agency. Moses and Pharaoh both speak directly (וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה לְפַרְעֹה - 'And Moses said to Pharaoh'; וַיֹּאמֶר לְמָחָר - 'And he said, Tomorrow'). Pharaoh exhibits emotional states and demonstrates volition through his refusal to comply (וְלֹא שָׁמַע אֲלֵהֶם - 'he did not listen'; וְלֹא אָבָה לְשַׁלְּחָם - 'he was not willing to let them go'). Aaron is also mentioned as a character who acts. These are mortal figures with agency, speech, and decision-making power, which constitutes lines, emotional states, and opinions.
